decisions.mark: states that a repository's own declared index_scope is preferred, and that every failure to find one falls through to indexing the whole repository
decisions.detail: QUOTE: A declared `index_scope` is used only if it is usable. ... A rejected declaration is refused at the CLI with exit 1 ... It is not silently widened. ... When nothing is declared ... The fallback is `whole_repo_scope` | WHY: The answer says a usable declared scope is used and that nothing declared falls back to the whole repo. But it says a rejected declaration is refused rather than widened, which contradicts "every failure falls through to whole-repo." || QUOTE: A declared `index_scope` is used only if it is usable. ... A rejected declaration is refused at the CLI with exit 1 ... It is not silently widened. ... The fallback is `whole_repo_scope` | WHY: The answer says that when nothing is declared the scope falls back to the whole repo. It also says a rejected declaration is refused, not widened. That contradicts the item's claim that every failure to find a declaration falls through to the whole repository. || QUOTE: A declared `index_scope` is used only if it is usable. ... A rejected declaration is refused at the CLI with exit 1 ... It is not silently widened. | WHY: The answer says that a rejected declaration is refused, not widened. That contradicts the item's claim that every failure to find a declaration falls through to indexing the whole repository. The answer's fallback applies only when nothing is declared, and it never says that failures fall through.

decisions.mark: conveys that the fallback carries a REASON explaining which scope was used and why, so an unstated scope is never silently guessed
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Log: the reason string records which tier was used and why, so the build log says "no index_scope is declared … the whole repository is the index scope". | WHY: The answer states the fallback scope carries a reason string recording which tier was used and why, so the choice is explicit rather than guessed. || QUOTE: Log: the reason string records which tier was used and why, so the build log says "no index_scope is declared … the whole repository is the index scope". | WHY: The answer says the fallback carries a reason string recording which tier was used and why, and that a rejected declaration is refused rather than silently widened. || QUOTE: "**Log:** the reason string records which tier was used and why, so the build log says "no index_scope is declared … the whole repository is the index scope"." | WHY: The answer states the fallback scope carries a reason string recording which tier was used and why, so scope isn't silently guessed.

decisions.mark: states that a Doxyfile's own INPUT is deliberately NOT used to decide the indexed tree, and explains why — a repository that ships one would get only its documented subset while a repository that ships none gets its whole tree
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The scope is then applied by `_fold_scope_into_args` (`cli.py:739`). It sets the INPUT to the root, sets EXCLUDE to the excludes, and sets `replace_input`, so the target Doxyfile's INPUT is discarded. | WHY: The answer says the target Doxyfile's INPUT is discarded, but it never explains why. The item requires the reason: a repo with a Doxyfile would get only its documented subset, while a repo without one would get its whole tree. || QUOTE: It sets the INPUT to the root, sets EXCLUDE to the excludes, and sets `replace_input`, so the target Doxyfile's INPUT is discarded. | WHY: The answer says the Doxyfile's INPUT is discarded, but it never explains the reason: that a repo shipping a Doxyfile would otherwise get only its documented subset while a repo without one gets its whole tree. || QUOTE: The scope is then applied by `_fold_scope_into_args` (`cli.py:739`). It sets the INPUT to the root, sets EXCLUDE to the excludes, and sets `replace_input`, so the target Doxyfile's INPUT is discarded. | WHY: The answer says the target Doxyfile's INPUT is discarded, but it never explains why. It doesn't say that using the Doxyfile's INPUT would give a repository that ships one only its documented subset, while a repository that ships none would get its whole tree.

decisions.mark: states that nested git trees are INDEXED and tagged rather than excluded from the scope
decisions.detail: QUOTE: **Nested trees:** they are indexed, not excluded (gh#333). `external.py` tags their rows afterwards so their files can be told apart. | WHY: The answer explicitly states nested git trees are indexed rather than excluded and that their rows are tagged afterwards. || QUOTE: "**Nested trees:** they are indexed, not excluded (gh#333). `external.py` tags their rows afterwards so their files can be told apart." | WHY: The answer explicitly states nested git trees are indexed rather than excluded and that their rows are tagged afterwards. || QUOTE: Nested trees: they are indexed, not excluded (gh#333). `external.py` tags their rows afterwards so their files can be told apart. | WHY: The answer explicitly says nested git trees are indexed rather than excluded and that their rows are tagged afterwards.

decisions.mark: states that the resolved scope is not the whole answer — within it, a file reaches the index only if something can read it, and names at least one of the two filters: the parse-built front end claiming the file types doxygen cannot read, or binary classification dropping files whose extension lies about them
